newsitem.title: FRANCE: Beluga flies chemical tank to Le Havre.
newsitem.headline: Beluga flies chemical tank to Le Havre.

text.p: Le Havre's Octeville airport said the first of 18 charter flights operated by Airbus Transport International (ATI), Super Transporter A300-600ST (ST) "Beluga" freighters will arrive later today, Tuesday.

"The Beluga is due in at 1340 local(1140 GMT) from Clermont-Ferrand in central France with a 38 tonne steel tank for a chemical ship being built by local shipbuilders, Ateliers et Chantiers du Havre" an airport spokesman told Reuters.
ATI is an Airbus Industrie subsidiary.

The steel tank -- 16.7 metres in length and 6.3 metres in diameter -- is being transported for a small French engineering company, the Societe Europeene de Chaudronnerie Industrielle (SECI), based 60 kilometres south-east from Clermont Ferrand at Brioude in the Haute-Loire.
Moving the tank is quicker and simpler than using road transport, industry sources said.
According to figures from France's airports authority federation, Le Havre handled only 29 tonnes of airfreight in 1996.

"Freight tonnage is negligible at present but the Beluga flight demonstrates to the region's shippers that Le Havre's airport is able handle full-freighter charters and there are air cargo solutions on their doorstep," the spokesman said.

"We do see some scope for developing intra-European all-cargo flights from Le Havre, mainly to the UK and northern Europe as well as to destinations in France." -- Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
